newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares end up ahead of Wall Street opening.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares end up ahead of Wall Street opening.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Monday in moderate trading as the market awaited Wall Street's opening, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.42 percent, or 0.85 points, to 205.65 on all-share turnover of 85 million shekels against 78 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 0.16 percent to 215.29.

"The market was rising on hopes that Wall Street stocks would rise today. The S&P 500 futures index rose and the American markets are expected to open higher," said Ari Eidelheit at Zeller Eblagon Securities.

"In the local market the indices are getting closer to their level at the beginning of the year and the mutual funds are trying to push them further up to show positive results at the end of the year," Eidelheit said.
"The mood in the market is good and the positive momentum continues. A rise in U.S. stocks will lead to a further rise in the local market," said Elisha Rosenfeld at Lehava Investments.

After the close of trading, the Israeli cabinet approved a further 1.2 billion shekel budget cut on top of the 4.9 billion shekels of cutbacks included in the original 1997 budget of 190.8 billion shekels.
"The approval of the budget will also help the market. Interest rates will decline and new money will come in," Rosenfeld said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which gained 0.75 percent to 27,875 on volume of 3.2 million shekels; Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 0.25 percent to 153,738 on turnover of 3.1 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which fell 0.5 percent to 287 on volume of 2.0 million shekels.
